To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the polypseudorotation of PEG-α-cyclodextrins with α- or γ-cyclodextrine formed the novel sustained release system for the pDNA.

the PEGylated α-cyD/polyamido amine dendrimer conjugates with CyD formed polypseudorotaaxanes, which provided sustained release of plasmid DNA from the complex at least for 72h in vitro and the transfection efficiency of PEGylated dendrimer/pDNA complex was sustained for at least 14 days by the formation of polypseudoroxanes with CyDs after intramuscular administration.
the PEGylated dendrimer conjugates with CyDs have a potential as the novel sustained release system of pDNA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel sustained release systems of pDNA for gene delivery.
the development of a sustained release system using the PEG- α-CDE/CyDS PPRX system for the nonviral gene delivery.
the preparation and characterization of PEG-α-CD/pDNA complexes and the PEG-CD/pDNA PPRX systems for the development of novel sustained DNA release and gene delivery systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CyD PPRX provided a novel sustained release system for pDNA from the PEG- α-CDE complex with DNA.
the CyDs PRRXs are useful as novel sustained release systems.

PEG-α-cyclodextrine/polyamidoamino dendrimer conjugates are able to form polypseudorotoraxanes (PPRx) with cyclodextrine solutions, which can be utilized as novel sustained release systems of plasmid DNA for DNA transfection in vivo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PEG-CyD/PEG-dendrimer PPRX system is useful for novel sustained release systems of pDNA.

the PEGylated dendrimer conjugated with CyD can form PPRXs in aqueous solutions and that the PPRX system can provide the sustained release of guest molecules from PEG-dendrimers complex with guest molecules.
the polypseudorotation of the polyamidoamine dendrimers with CyDs is a powerful method to form PPRXs, and the CyDs PRRXs are useful for sustained release of pDNAs in vitro and in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can control the release time of the plasmid DNA by changing the volume of the dissolution medium and the type of the CyD.
the PEG-CyD/PEG-dendrimer PPRX system has the potential to be applied for the sustained release systems of pDNA and other macromolecules.

the PEGylated α-CyD/polyamido amine (PAMAM) dendrimer conjugates can form polypseudoroxanes with α-CyDs or γ-CyDs, but not β-CyDs, and the polypseudororotaxanes provide the sustained release of plasmid DNA from PEGylated dendrimer complex.
